files.about.txt:
Nicholas V. Giamblanco
Compiler Engineer · Coquitlam, British Columbia, Canada
========================================================================

I'm a compiler engineer who builds languages, compilers and tooling for
hardware accelerators.

Today I'm a Senior Member of Technical Staff in Advanced Tech. R&D at
Cerebras Systems, where I design a data-flow language and compiler for
the Wafer-Scale Engine (WSE).

My training is in high-level synthesis (HLS): my M.A.Sc. at the
University of Toronto, with Prof. Jason H. Anderson, focused on dynamic
memory allocation for HLS in LegUp.

Interests:
  * compilers (LLVM, MLIR, CIRCT)
  * data-flow and wafer-scale computing
  * high-level synthesis
  * hardware verification and simulation
  * debuggers and developer tooling

GitHub:   https://github.com/ngiambla
Web:      https://ngiambla.github.io/
From:     Arnprior, Ontario
files.cv.txt:
Nicholas V. Giamblanco
========================================================================

EXPERIENCE
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Cerebras Systems, Coquitlam, BC
  Senior Member of Technical Staff, Advanced Tech. R&D  (Sep 2024 - present)
    - Designing a user-friendly data-flow language and compiler that
      raises the abstraction level for programming Cerebras' Wafer-Scale
      Engines.
    - Built a register allocator that cut code size and improved runtime
      performance by 40% on average.
    - Built a methodology to connect and manage hundreds of WSEs at high
      throughput and bandwidth.
    - Built a spatial-temporal reservation system for multi-tenancy
      across many WSEs.
    - Introduced a hardware debugger for the WSE; deployed R&D tooling
      to national lab partners (NETL, Sandia).

Cerebras Systems, Coquitlam, BC
  Senior Member of Technical Staff, Strategic Initiatives  (Jun 2024 - Sep 2024)
    - Compiler and runtime optimizations for the world's fastest LLM
      inference.
    - Introduced a neural-network-compiler fuzzer for inference and
      training flows.

Rain AI, Coquitlam, BC
  Staff Compiler Engineer  (Mar 2024 - Jun 2024)
    - Compiled neural networks for a compute-in-memory RISC-V edge
      device with MLIR and LLVM.
    - Implemented a path to fully use RISC-V's RVV vector extension.

Micron Technology, Coquitlam, BC
  Principal Compiler Engineer, Silicon-Systems AI  (Apr 2022 - Mar 2024)
    - Hardware design-verification techniques that find bugs up to 16x
      faster.
    - Automatic RTL co-simulation environment with up to 76x less
      simulation time (innovation award).
    - A compiler infrastructure for hardware static analysis, 5x faster
      than commercial tools.

Cerebras Systems, Toronto, ON
  Member of Technical Staff  (Aug 2020 - Apr 2022)
    - Core compiler and runtime features for the Weight-Streaming
      product, plus a Weight-Streaming tensor debugger.
    - A replay debugger for the CS-1 with reverse debugging, value
      tracking and profiling, used company-wide.
    - Random-program test infrastructure for the LLVM backend; compiler
      passes that improved code by 10%.

Untether AI, Toronto, ON
  Compiler Engineer  (Jan 2020 - Aug 2020)
    - Principal engineer for the LLVM compiler backend, delivered 6
      months ahead of schedule.

Information Sciences Institute (USC), Arlington, VA and Toronto, ON
  Visiting Research Assistant, then Researcher  (Jun 2019 - Jun 2020)
    - Project REAPER: an HDL-to-LLVM compiler.
    - Sped up an algorithm in a NASA project by 30,000x with high-level
      synthesis.

EDUCATION
------------------------------------------------------------------------
University of Toronto (2019)
  M.A.Sc., Electrical & Computer Engineering
  Thesis: Dynamic Memory Allocation Techniques for High-Level Synthesis.
  Supervisor: Prof. Jason H. Anderson.

Ryerson University (2017)
  B.Eng., Electrical & Computer Engineering
